newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unions call new public transport strike.
newsitem.headline: French unions call new public transport strike.

text.p: France's three biggest trade unions called on Friday a new day of strikes and protests for February 28 in public transport in cities across the country except Paris.

The pro-Socialist CFDT, Communist CGT and non-partisan Force Ouvriere jointly called the protests, to be defined by local branches, to press demands for a cut in working hours and for early retirement.
A strike movement launched in late January in Toulouse and this month in about 20 other cities has crumbled and hit only four towns on Friday.
Force Ouvriere last week called for the protests to stop but on Friday it hardened its stance after talks with bosses.
The southern cities of Nice, Cannes, Clermont-Ferrand and Sete are still hit by the strikes which disrupted buses, trams and Metro underground railways.
The unions have won concessions on working hours but employers have not given in to union calls to cut the retirement age to 55 years from 60.

The strikes are the latest labour challenge to the centre-right government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe, which last year bowed to truckers' demands for retirement at 55 after they blocked roads. The government has said that the state pension system would be bankrupted if all workers retired at 55.
